name: genuine index-unknown caveat survives alongside a null-caveat hedge phrased without the word 'null'
description: task-m2-python-preset.md stage 6 addendum 3: 'MASK' - a response that has BOTH index_state_unknown (indexingStatus: unknown) AND provider_null_incoming_calls in limitationDetails at once (the two are independent axes and can co-occur). The summary correctly discloses both: a genuine index-completeness caveat ('the index may not cover every file') and the null-caveat hedge surfaced via 'dependency injection' (no 'null' word anywhere). The marker-anchored fix (widening the exclusion anchor to all four provider_null_incoming_calls phrases, still requiring the marker nearby) broke this: once 'dependency injection' became a recognized marker, the exclusion span grew to swallow 'not evidence that no caller exists — check dependency injection' whole, and because the genuine index caveat ('may not cover every file') sat right next to it with no separator recognized by the old INDEX_UNCERTAINTY_PATTERN, the ENTIRE index-uncertainty signal in this summary was lost - producing missing_index_caveat AND missing_high_severity_disclosure (for index_state_unknown) together, since both route through mentionsIndexUncertainty(). Reconstructing that fix and running it against this exact response/summary confirms both would fire (non-vacuity). The real fix (1) excludes 'not evidence/proof ... no caller(s) exist(s)' unconditionally, without needing any marker word nearby, so the swallowed span shrinks back to just that clause, and (2) widens INDEX_UNCERTAINTY_PATTERN to recognize 'may not cover/include/reflect/capture' as a genuine index-uncertainty phrase in its own right, so it no longer depends on surviving next to a null-caveat marker by accident. Must-pass fixture 15.
